title: Conditional transport of the sections unit along the canonical affine isomorphism
statement: Let S be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], with independently chosen derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], and C any unbounded cochain complex of module sheaves on X = Spec Γ(S, top). Let E be restriction along S.toSpecΓ, assumed additive, and G be global sections on X followed by restriction of scalars along (ΓSpecIso Γ(S, top)).inv. If the right-derived functor unit of G at the homotopy quotient of C is invertible, then the right-derived global-sections unit on S at the homotopy quotient of E(C) is invertible [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. No quasi-coherence, tilde presentation, or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06Z0, identification of derived global sections; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06Z0; equivalence transport argument written by F1

proof.text: Construct the restriction equivalence E using restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId for S.toSpecΓ and its inverse. Independently construct the equivalence of pushforward functors along this isomorphism. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies E with pushforward along the inverse. Evaluation at top then gives E followed by global sections on S naturally isomorphic to G. The scalar actions agree because (inv S.toSpecΓ).appTop = inv S.toSpecΓ.appTop and toSpecΓ_appTop identifies the latter inverse with ΓSpecIso.inv. This is implemented by the proved private constructions affineRestrictionEquivalence and affineSectionsIso.

Take a K-injective resolution s : C → I, using the sheaf-module Grothendieck instance and the existing HasKInjectiveResolutions API. The proved private criterion unit_iso_iff_resolution follows from naturality of the right-derived unit: its component at I is invertible, and the right-derived functor sends Qh(s) to an isomorphism, so its component at C is invertible exactly when Qh(F(s)) is. Apply this to G and the supplied hypothesis. Map the sections natural isomorphism to homotopy categories and postcompose with Qh; NatIso.isIso_map_iff transports invertibility of G(s) to (E followed by sections)(s). The homotopy-category composition isomorphism identifies this with sections(E(s)). Since the additive equivalence E preserves K-injectivity and quasi-isomorphisms, the same criterion for global sections on S and E(s) gives the conclusion. This uses only naturality and localization for the chosen derived categories, with no comparison of arbitrary chosen resolution objects.

theorem affineSectionsUnit_transport (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S]
    [(Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor S.toSpecΓ).Additive]
    (C : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec Γ(S, ⊤)).toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (h : IsIso ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor (Spec Γ(S, ⊤)).toRingedSpace ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(S, ⊤)).inv.hom).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj C))) :
    IsIso ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor S.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor S.toSpecΓ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)))
